purpose: Issue one append-only successor to the immutable v3 runtime-correction authority after real CUA execution exposed exactly two remaining read-only fixture defects: the successful owner GET returned an API success envelope although the sealed HRM-009 query adapter consumes a raw Hrm009Projection, and semantically equal PAGE evidence or trusted-scope values could acquire new JavaScript object identities and repeatedly trigger DATA evaluation or owner GET. This v4 authorizes only the raw fixture projection correction, HRM-009-local primitive and memo stability, the matching targeted tests, one CUA stability observation, and the first execution of the already dedicated five-row browser matrix. It does not activate or enroll a tenant, enable or exercise a writable action, use customer or production data, or close HRM-009, Batch-03, or R7.

v4OverridesOnly: successful fixture owner GET response shape
HRM-009-local semantic primitive and memo stability for DATA evaluation and owner GET
the bounded verification set after these two corrections

observationAOwnerProjectionShape.rootCause: The fixture success helper wrapped the projection as {status,message,data}, while queryHrm009Entry passes response.data directly to selectHrm009Projection and that sealed parser requires the raw top-level Hrm009Projection fields.
observationAOwnerProjectionShape.securityInterpretation: This is a fixture response-shape mismatch after a trusted read-only GET. It is not permission to weaken the production projection parser, accept an additive envelope, alter an owner endpoint, or expose additional fields.

observationBSemanticIdentityChurn.observedEffect: DATA evaluation and owner GET could repeat while the admitted route, query, scope primitives, decision revision, locale, time zone, correlation identifier, cursor and adapter were semantically unchanged.
observationBSemanticIdentityChurn.rootCause: A DATA admission effect could depend on a newly created PAGE-evidence object and the certificate query load callback could depend on a newly created trusted-scope object. React reference equality therefore treated semantically equal values as new dependencies.
observationBSemanticIdentityChurn.securityInterpretation: The correction must stabilize only the existing trusted primitives. It must not cache across scope or revision changes, suppress lease renewal, reuse a correlation identifier across a changed semantic identity, or weaken fail-closed admission.

correctionAFixtureRawOwnerProjection.authorizedBehaviorChange: For a valid GET to either sealed HRM-009 owner path, return HTTP 200 with the raw Hrm009Projection object as the JSON response body instead of wrapping it in the fixture success envelope.

successResponseContract.consumer: queryHrm009Entry response.data passed directly to selectHrm009Projection

unchangedBoundaries: invalid contextScopeKey or correlationId still fails closed
scenario-specific COMPLETE, EMPTY, PARTIAL and UNAVAILABLE projection contents remain sealed
owner GET counters and monotonic events remain sanitized
POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and step-up remain denied and counted
no production API or backend source is changed

routeAdmissionContract.authorizedTechnique: Extract the trusted PAGE evidence primitives and use those primitives plus the existing semantic identity as effect dependencies; memoize the admitted Hrm009TrustedScope from its exact primitive tuple.
routeAdmissionContract.forbiddenDependencyTrigger: A new PAGE-evidence or trusted-scope object reference with all sealed primitive values unchanged must not by itself trigger another DATA evaluation or owner GET.
routeAdmissionContract.correlationIdRule: Retain one correlation identifier while the semantic DATA admission identity is unchanged and issue a new identifier when that semantic identity changes.
routeAdmissionContract.leaseRule: Existing lease renewal and expiry behavior remains authoritative and may trigger a fresh DATA evaluation only through the existing evaluation generation or a changed semantic identity.

workbenchQueryContract.authorizedTechnique: Use HRM-009-local primitive dependencies or an HRM-009-local memoized trusted-scope value so the query callback is stable when the semantic scope tuple is unchanged.
workbenchQueryContract.staleRequestPolicy: Abort the superseded request and never apply a response from a superseded semantic identity.

requiredTargetedTests: Route-admission test rerenders semantically equal PAGE and request-scope values through new object identities and proves exactly one DATA evaluation for the unchanged identity.
Route-admission test proves a changed trusted primitive or the existing lease-renewal generation still causes the required fresh evaluation and remains fail closed.
Certificate-workbench test rerenders with a new trusted-scope object containing the same five primitive values and proves no duplicate owner GET.
Certificate-workbench test proves a changed semantic scope primitive causes one fresh owner GET and the superseded in-flight request cannot publish state.

cuaStabilityGate.precondition: Reset the dedicated fixture counters, use the already authenticated dedicated local runtime, and navigate once to the canonical personal route without exercising any action.
requiredUiState: the COMPLETE personal projection is visible
cuaStabilityGate.stabilityObservation: After the workbench settles, take two sanitized fixture-counter snapshots separated by a no-user-action accessibility and visual observation. The PAGE, DATA, owner GET, mutation, step-up and unexpected counters and the last monotonic event sequence must remain identical between snapshots.
forbiddenDuringObservation: fixture reset between the two snapshots
cuaStabilityGate.defaultOffReason: The checked-in default-OFF observation was already completed under v3 and this successor changes no checked-in runtime default or enrollment state.

firstFiveRowMatrixGate.failurePolicy: Stop on the first failed result, preserve sanitized evidence, and require a new append-only authority before any replay. Do not rerun passing rows or substitute a broader suite.

frontend.worktreeNote: The authority binds the exact committed base. Shared uncommitted candidate changes and evidence present during issuance are not treated as prior authorization or as committed evidence.

forbidden: Changing a source or test file outside the exact six-file implementation allowlist
Changing the production Hrm009Projection wire contract or weakening selectHrm009Projection to accept an envelope
Caching or reusing authority, projections, correlation identifiers or requests across a changed tenant, actor, route, query, scope, decision revision, locale, time zone, cursor or adapter
Suppressing legitimate lease renewal, expiry, scope change, route change, pagination or explicit refresh
Disabling React StrictMode, authorization validation, abort handling or fail-closed concealment
Changing the dedicated Playwright config, package.json, a lockfile, migration, checked-in runtime default, activation or enrollment
Logging credentials, cookies, Authorization headers, raw request bodies or other secrets
Executing a repository-wide suite, a broad browser replay, or the complete five-row matrix more than once
Enabling or exercising a writable HRM-009 action, step-up, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE
Claiming download, revoke, verification, expiry, access-audit, download-audit, persistent activation, enrollment or production release
Treating fixture or browser-gate evidence as business completion credit
